Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 87, verse 1:

﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High﴾ i.e., exalt your Lord above what is not befitting to Him, and "name" is a superfluous (zā'id) element; "the Most High" (al-A'lā) is an attribute (ṣifah) of "your Lord."

Commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on Surah 87, verse 2:

﴿Who created and proportioned﴾ [His] creation. He made it proportionate in its parts, without disparity.
And ﴿He who decreed﴾ what He willed, ﴿and then guided﴾ to what He had decreed of good and evil.

**Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah al-A'la (87), verse 4:**

﴿And He who brings forth the pasture﴾ — He makes the herbage grow.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on surah 87, verse 5:

﴿Then He made it﴾ after the greenness, ﴿into dry stubble﴾ dry and crumbled, ﴿dark brown﴾ black and dry.
﴿We will make you recite﴾ the Qur'an, ﴿so you will not forget﴾ what you recite.

Except what Allah wills, [that] you should forget it, by abrogating its recitation and its ruling. The Messenger (ﷺ) used to recite aloud along with Jibril's recitation out of fear of forgetting, so it was as if he were told: "Do not hasten with it, for you will not forget. So do not tire yourself by reciting it aloud." ﴿Indeed He﴾ (exalted is He) ﴿knows what is manifest﴾ of speech and action ﴿and what is hidden﴾ of them.
﴿And We will ease you toward ease﴾ for the easy sharia (the revealed law), which is Islam.

Translation of the commentary on Surah 87 (al-A'la), verse 9:

﴿So remind﴾: admonish with the Qur'an. ﴿if the reminder benefits﴾: "if" here is in the sense of "although" or "whether," referring to the reminder mentioned in ﴿he will remember﴾ (sayadhdhakkaru), meaning: even if it does not benefit. Its benefit is for some, and the lack of benefit is for others.
﴿He will be mindful﴾ [of the reminder] by it, ﴿the one who fears﴾ [fears God Most High], as in the verse
﴿And the most wretched will avoid it﴾ — i.e., the reminder; he leaves it aside, paying it no heed. ﴿The most wretched﴾ — in the sense of the wretched one, i.e., the disbeliever.
Those who will burn in the greatest Fire. The Great Fire is the Fire of the Hereafter, and the lesser Fire is the Fire of this world.
Then he will neither die therein" so that he may find rest, "nor live" a life of ease.

(Surah 87, verse 14)

﴿Indeed, he has succeeded﴾ means he has won (faza), ﴿who purifies himself﴾ means he has cleansed himself (tataharra) by faith.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 87, verse 15:

﴿And he remembers the name of his Lord﴾ [saying] "Allahu akbar" (God is greatest), ﴿and prays﴾ the five daily prayers. And that is among the matters of the Hereafter, while the disbelievers of Makkah turn away from it.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn on surah 87, verse 16:

﴿Nay, but you prefer﴾ with the taa' (second person) and the yaa' (third person) read: ﴿the worldly life﴾ over ﴿the Hereafter﴾.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 87, verse 17:

﴿And the Hereafter﴾, which comprises Paradise, ﴿is better and more enduring﴾.

Tafsir al-Jalalayn (al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on surah 87, verse 18:

﴿Indeed, this﴾ — the success of the one who purifies himself, and that the Hereafter is better — ﴿is in the former scriptures﴾, i.e., those revealed before the Qur'an.

Scriptures of Ibrahim (Abraham) and Musa (Moses). These were ten scrolls of Ibrahim, and the Torah of Musa.

Note on the translation: the source text is a single sentence with no commentary beyond the verse, so it has been translated as it stands.
